title: Enterprise onboarding, escalation, integration, health-checks & QBR playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard operating procedure for enterprise onboarding, integration, escalation response, routine health checks, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) preparation. It is intended for Customer Success, Support Engineers, Solutions Engineers, and cross-functional stakeholders (Product, SRE, Eng). Follow this guide to ensure consistent onboarding outcomes, fast resolution of customer-impacting issues, and repeatable QBRs that drive adoption and retention.

Key goals
- Accelerate time-to-value for enterprise customers (goal: production-ready within 6-8 weeks for standard integrations).
- Provide a clear escalation path and SLOs for support response and resolution.
- Standardize integration tasks and known-issue workarounds to reduce repeat tickets.
- Produce actionable QBRs and health checks aligned to customer KPIs.

Owners and roles
- Customer Success (CS) Manager: primary relationship owner; coordinates onboarding milestones and QBRs.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical lead for integration, onboarding runbooks, and initial validation.
- Support Engineer (L2): triage, diagnostics, and working with Eng/SRE for escalations.
- Support Engineering Manager / Oncall Eng (L3): takes ownership for P1/P0 incidents and cross-team coordination.
- Product / Eng: feature or model changes required for long-term fixes.

Onboarding timeline & milestones (standard enterprise)
1. Kickoff (week 0)
   - Deliverables: NDA/compliance checklist, contact matrix, initial data handling requirements.
   - CS schedules kickoff call; SE prepares integration checklist.
2. Integration & connectivity (weeks 1-2)
   - Deliverables: API keys, network allowlists, test account access, sandbox model catalog.
   - SE performs handshake test: auth, simple generate, embedding, and streaming.
3. Performance & capacity planning (weeks 2-3)
   - Deliverables: traffic profile, expected qps, latency targets, recommended Dedicated sizing if needed.
   - Run standard perf tests: 95th/99th latency at target qps; provide suggested batching/quantization profile.
4. Security & compliance (weeks 2-4)
   - Deliverables: SOC/ISO evidence, KMS integration plan, data residency confirmation.
5. Pilot / validation (weeks 3-6)
   - Deliverables: pilot run, success metrics, known-issue checklist.
6. Production cutover & QBR prep (week 6-8)
   - Deliverables: production keys, runbook handoff, agreed SLOs and monitoring dashboards.

Pre-integration checklist (SE)
- Confirm API access: customer org id, environment (sandbox/prod), and initial API key.
- Network & firewall: IP ranges allowlisted (see infra page) and VPC peering details if private deployment.
- Model selection & config: model variant, max tokens, temperature, streaming enabled/disabled.
- Data handling: logging level, PII redaction policy, KMS/HSM key ownership.
- Monitoring hooks: Datadog/Grafana metrics endpoints, prefix for customer tags.

Integration quickstart (step-by-step)
1. Create sandbox API key and confirm token works:
   - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/test -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>"
2. Basic generation smoke test:
   - curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Hello"}'
3. Validate streaming & chunking: enable `stream=true` and confirm partial responses arrive within expected intervals.
4. Run embedding sanity check: submit 10 sample sentences and verify vector dimensions match model spec.
5. Validate rate limits and quotas: request large batch and confirm 429 behavior and backoff headers.

Support process & ticketing standards
- Primary system: Zendesk (internal piping to CS Slack #support-escalations).
- Ticket triage (first 30 minutes): confirm severity, gather logs (request_id/x-request-id), customer timestamp, API request payloads (redact PII), and observed behaviour.
- Severity definitions: see Escalation Matrix section below.
- Required ticket fields: customer_org_id, environment, endpoint, sample request/response, first_seen, impact_description, tentative owner.

Escalation matrix and SLOs
- Sev 0 / P0 (Platform outage – customer-facing production down):
  - Response target: 15 minutes
  - Next steps: Pager notify (oncall Eng), incident bridge within 30 mins, customer exec update every 60 mins.
- Sev 1 / P1 (Severe degradation – high error rates or latency > SLO):
  - Response target: 30 minutes
  - Next steps: CS and Support Engineering owned; engage Eng/SRE within 60 mins if no mitigation.
- Sev 2 / P2 (Partial impact – feature broken for subset):
  - Response target: 4 business hours
  - Next steps: Triage by Support Engineer; scheduled maintenance window if needed.
- Sev 3 / P3 (General question / minor issue):
  - Response target: 2 business days
  - Next steps: Standard support ticket flow.

Escalation steps (numbered)
1. Triage & collect artifacts: request_id, region, model, request body, response headers, and timestamps.
2. Reproduce in sandbox (if safe) and capture deterministic steps.
3. Attempt mitigation: fallback model variant, throttling, increase replica count (Dedicated), or rolling restart.
4. If not resolved within response target for severity, escalate to L3 with a consolidated packet (summary, logs, reproduction).
5. For P0/P1: open incident bridge, assign incident commander (IC), and route updates to exec sponsor and Customer Success.

Known issues & workarounds (common categories)
- 429 / rate-limit spikes:
  - Symptoms: intermittent 429s at traffic bursts.
  - Workaround: implement client-side exponential backoff w/ jitter; set per-route client quotas.
  - Long-term: enable Dedicated capacity or configure burst capacity.
- High tail latency on long context windows:
  - Symptoms: 95th/99th latency spikes when max_tokens + prompt_length > 8k.
  - Workaround: reduce requested max_tokens, enable prefix caching, or select a model optimized for long contexts.
- Streaming connection drops (websocket/timeouts):
  - Symptoms: partial responses, aborted streams.
  - Workaround: increase connection keepalive, verify reverse proxies (NGINX) support chunked transfer; retry stream from last token using KV cache continuation.
- Embedding dimension mismatch errors:
  - Symptoms: client receives unexpected vector length.
  - Workaround: confirm model_id and version; regenerate sample embeddings in sandbox and update client vector processing.

Health checks, monitoring & dashboards
- Standard dashboards to provide to customer during handoff:
  - Traffic overview: qps, 5m/1h rolling average, error rate, 95th/99th latency per model.
  - Cost & token usage: tokens per request breakdown and monthly projection.
  - Cache hit rate: prefix/KV cache hits and effective latency savings.
  - Model fallbacks & routing events: counts and reasons.
- Recommended Datadog queries (examples):
  - Errors: sum:requests.errors{customer:ORG_ID} by {code}.as_count()
  - Latency (p95):pct(95,requests.latency_ms{customer:ORG_ID})

QBR cadence and agenda (quarterly)
- Attendees: CS Manager, Customer Engineering lead, Customer PM/Prod owner, Engagement Executive, 1-2 Product/SRE reps as needed.
- Pre-meeting deliverables (two weeks prior): health report, usage trends, top 10 prompt regressions, cost vs forecast, and FYI roadmap items.
- Typical agenda (60-90 mins):
  1. Exec summary & topline metrics (5-10 mins)
  2. Adoption & feature usage (10-15 mins)
  3. Performance & reliability review (10-20 mins)
  4. Cost optimization & recommendations (10-15 mins)
  5. Open risks / action items / roadmap alignment (15-20 mins)
- Follow-up: publish minutes, owners, and target dates in customer workspace within 48 hours.

Templates and examples
- Support ticket summary template:
  - Subject: [SEV1] High error rate on /v1/generate for org <ORG_ID>
  - Body: Impact, first_seen, last_seen, reproduction steps, request_id(s), environment, temporary mitigation applied.
- QBR one-pager template: includes topline metrics (qps, cost, SLO attainment), 3 wins, 3 risks, recommended next steps.

Operational runbook snippets
- For 429 flood mitigation (quick commands):
  1) Identify spike: curl 'https://internal-metrics.local/api?org=<ORG>&metric=requests.rate'
  2) Throttle at edge: update rate-limit rule in Kong: 
     - kubectl exec -n kong $(kubectl get pod -n kong -l app=kong -o name | head -n1) -- kong config db_import /tmp/new_config.yml
  3) Notify CS and set customer rate_limit_override flag.

Postmortem & RCA expectations
- For any Sev0/P0 incident involving a customer, publish a postmortem within 7 business days. Postmortem must include: timeline, impact, mitigation steps, root cause, corrective actions, owners, and follow-up verification plan.

Handover checklist (to SRE/Platform for production)
- Dashboards provisioned with customer tag.
- Alert thresholds configured: error rate > 1% sustained for 5 mins; p95 latency > agreed SLO + 50% sustained 10 mins.
- Runbooks linked in incident response channel and customer workspace.

Appendix: useful contacts
- Customer Success general: cs-team@redwood.ai
- Enterprise Support (L2): support-enterprise@redwood.ai
- Oncall Eng (L3): pager duty link in team wiki (see related pages)
- Solutions Engineering: solutions-eng@redwood.ai

Revision history
- 2025-11-01: Created by Ava Martinez.
- 2026-03-20: Added known-issues section and streaming troubleshooting by Priya Patel.
- 2026-06-15: Published canonical playbook and QBR templates; reviewers: Liam O'Connor, Marcus Chen.

Notes
- Keep customer-specific variations documented in the customer workspace (Confluence space per account). This playbook defines the company-wide default process.
